title: Columnstore fact query that reads every row group
prompt: Store sales dashboard for a date range, usually the last 30 days. Each call uses about 38 s of CPU at DOP 8. Plan:
Columnstore Index Scan of CCI_FactSales in batch mode; all 1,400 row groups are read and none is eliminated. The two
DATEDIFF predicates are not pushed into the scan: a Filter above the scan evaluates them for all 1.4B rows. SaleDate
is a date column, and both parameters are date. The API validates both dates to the years 2000 to 2100 and never
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.
FactSales: 1.4B rows in a clustered columnstore index, ~1,400 row groups. Rows are loaded once a day in SaleDate order, so each row group holds a narrow SaleDate range.
baseline_sql: SELECT f.StoreID, SUM(f.Quantity) AS Units, SUM(f.NetAmount) AS Net

correct_families.description: Compare the column itself with the two dates. The predicate is pushed into the scan and only the row groups whose SaleDate range overlaps are read.
reference_sql: SELECT f.StoreID, SUM(f.Quantity) AS Units, SUM(f.NetAmount) AS Net

traps.why: The original includes @To. SaleDate < @To drops the last day of the range.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case one_day: the baseline returns that day's sales, the rewrite returns no rows.
example_sql: SELECT f.StoreID, SUM(f.Quantity) AS Units, SUM(f.NetAmount) AS Net

traps.why: Another function on SaleDate is as opaque to the scan as DATEDIFF: no predicate pushdown and no row group elimination.
example_sql: SELECT f.StoreID, SUM(f.Quantity) AS Units, SUM(f.NetAmount) AS Net
WHERE CONVERT(char(8), f.SaleDate, 112) BETWEEN CONVERT(char(8), @From, 112) AND CONVERT(char(8), @To, 112)

traps.why: A rowstore index on SaleDate over 1.4B rows costs load time and space, and a 30-day range through it is slower than the eliminated columnstore scan.

min_improvement.basis: About 30 of 1,400 row groups hold a 30-day range, because rows are loaded in SaleDate order.
